We installed call tracking for a personal injury firm last month.

They thought their Google Ads weren't working. "The leads are garbage," they said. They were about to cancel their $6,000/month ad spend.

The data told a different story:

90 calls came in from Google Ads. 34 went straight to voicemail. 22 calls rang for more than 30 seconds before someone picked up — only 9 callers waited that long. The rest hung up.

The math is brutal: If your intake team answers in 30 seconds instead of 10, you lose half your leads. If calls go to voicemail after hours, you lose 100% of them.

days.email_subject: The 60-second rule (and the $127K it cost one firm)
days.email_body:
A workers' comp firm in Texas lost $127,000 last year.

Not to bad ads. Not to a competitor's better website. They lost it to slow intake.

We ran the numbers: Their average time to answer a call was 3 minutes 14 seconds. During business hours. After hours, most calls went to voicemail and got returned the next morning.

Here's what we found when we analyzed 90 days of call data across 11 law firms:

Answer time under 60 seconds: 34% conversion rate (caller becomes signed case)
Answer time 60-180 seconds: 19% conversion rate
Answer time over 3 minutes: 8% conversion rate

Same traffic source. Same lead quality. Same practice areas. The ONLY variable was how fast someone picked up the phone.

Why does this happen? Because the person calling you is also calling 3 other firms. In personal injury, criminal defense, and family law, the first firm to answer gets the case 78% of the time.

The fix isn't complicated, but it requires three things:

1. A dedicated intake line that routes to multiple people simultaneously (not a receptionist who's also doing 4 other jobs)
2. After-hours coverage — either an overflow service or rotating on-call staff
3. Call tracking that measures ring time, not just "calls received"

We'll show you exactly how to set this up tomorrow.

For now: Pull your call log from last month. How many calls came in after 5pm? How many went to voicemail? Multiply that number by your average case value. That's what slow intake is costing you.

We installed call tracking and found the problem immediately: 67% of calls that came in after 5pm went to voicemail. In criminal defense, that's a disaster — someone just got arrested. They're calling from jail. They need a lawyer NOW, not tomorrow morning.

Every missed call was a $4,800 case (their average) walking to a competitor.

The fix cost $247/month:

1. Call routing software (CallRail): $45/month. Routes calls to 3 staff members simultaneously. If no one picks up in 15 seconds, it overflows to the answering service.

2. After-hours answering service (Ruby Receptionists): $200/month for 50 calls. A live person answers, qualifies the lead, and texts the intake team immediately.

3. Automated SMS for missed calls (Lawmatics, which they already had): "We got your call. An attorney will call you back within 15 minutes." This alone recovered 11 cases in the first month.

The result: 94% of after-hours calls now get answered within 60 seconds. Signed cases went from 9/month to 23/month in 90 days.

ROI: 26:1 in month one.

You don't need to hire a night shift. You don't need a massive budget. You need three tools and two hours to set them up.

days.email_subject: How one immigration firm went from 4 cases/month to 32
days.email_body:
In March, Mandall Law signed 4 immigration cases.

By September, they signed 32.

Same Google Ads budget ($4,000/month). Same traffic volume. Same practice area.

What changed? We rebuilt their intake system.

Before we started:
- Calls came into a shared office line that also handled client questions, vendor calls, and everything else
- Average answer time: 4 minutes 18 seconds
- After-hours (5pm-9am): voicemail, returned the next business day
- No call tracking, no idea which leads came from ads vs referrals vs organic

The result: They were paying $87 per click on Google Ads, getting 60-70 calls/month, but only converting 6-7% into signed cases.

Here's what we fixed:

1. Dedicated intake line. New phone number used ONLY for marketing leads (not existing clients). Tracked in CallRail so we could see source, recording, and answer time for every call.

2. Speed to lead system. Calls route to 3 intake specialists simultaneously. If no answer in 15 seconds, overflow to Ruby Receptionists. Target: under 60 seconds, every time.

3. After-hours coverage. Instead of voicemail, overflow service answers 5pm-9am. They qualify the lead ("What country are you from? What visa are you applying for?") and text the intake team. Follow-up happens within 15 minutes, even at 11pm.

4. Instant SMS for missed calls. If someone does slip through, they get an automated text: "We got your call. An immigration attorney will call you back within 15 minutes."

The result after 6 months:
- Answer time: 58 seconds average
- After-hours answer rate: 91% (up from 0%)
- Conversion rate: 34% (up from 6%)
- Revenue: $92,000/month from a $4,000/month ad budget

This wasn't about better ads or a new website. It was about picking up the phone faster.

Tomorrow: I'll send you the exact tools, costs, and setup process (step-by-step) so you can replicate this.
